SCI-15.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the photosynthesis equation, where oxygen comes from, which metal is in chlorophyll, plant hormones and their jobs, stomata/transpiration, modified stems and roots (potato, ginger, sweet potato), and famous botanists.

## Photosynthesis (সালোকসংশ্লেষণ) 🔥🔥
**6CO₂ + 12H₂O → (sunlight, chlorophyll) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + 6H₂O**

- Green plants make **glucose** from **carbon dioxide and water** using **sunlight**; **oxygen** is released. Energy change: **light → chemical energy**.
- Takes place in the **chloroplast**, mainly in **leaves** (the **"food factory"** of the plant; mesophyll cells).
- The **oxygen released comes from water**, not from CO₂ (proved with isotope ¹⁸O by Ruben and Kamen).
- **Chlorophyll** contains **magnesium (Mg)**. It absorbs mostly **red and blue light** and **reflects green**, so leaves look green. Photosynthesis is **least in green light**.
- Two phases:
  - **Light reaction** — in the **grana (thylakoids)**; water splits (**photolysis**), O₂ and ATP/NADPH form.
  - **Dark reaction (Calvin cycle)** — in the **stroma**; CO₂ is fixed into sugar. Worked out by **Melvin Calvin** (Nobel 1961).
- Glucose is stored as **starch**. **Iodine test**: starch turns **blue-black**.
- Factors: light, CO₂, temperature, water, chlorophyll.
- Maize, sugarcane are **C₄ plants** (efficient in hot climates); rice, wheat are C₃.
- **Respiration** is the reverse: food + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + energy; it happens **day and night** in all living cells.

## Water, stomata and transport 🔥
- **Stomata (পত্ররন্ধ্র)**: tiny pores mostly on the **lower surface of leaves**, controlled by **guard cells**; used for **gas exchange** and **transpiration**.
- **Transpiration (প্রস্বেদন)**: loss of water vapour from leaves; it cools the plant and creates **"transpiration pull"** that lifts water.
- **Roots** absorb water by **osmosis** through root hairs. **Xylem** carries water up; **phloem** carries food.
- **Mangrove** plants (**Sundarbans**) have **pneumatophores (breathing roots, শ্বাসমূল)** because the mud lacks oxygen. The main tree of the Sundarbans is **Sundari (Heritiera fomes)**.

## Plant hormones (উদ্ভিদ হরমোন) 🔥
| Hormone | Main role |
|---|---|
| **Auxin** (first discovered; F. W. Went, 1928) | Growth of stem/root tip, **phototropism** (bending toward light), rooting of cuttings, seedless fruit |
| **Gibberellin** | **Stem elongation**, bolting, seed germination, larger fruit |
| **Cytokinin** | **Cell division**, delays ageing of leaves |
| **Ethylene** (a gas) | **Fruit ripening** |
| **Abscisic acid (ABA)** | **"Stress hormone"**; closes stomata, causes **dormancy and leaf fall** |

- **Florigen** is the proposed flowering hormone. **Photoperiodism**: flowering depends on day length.
- **Parthenocarpy**: fruit without fertilisation → **seedless** fruit (banana, seedless grapes).

## Modified parts (what we eat) 🔥
| Plant | Part eaten / modification |
|---|---|
| **Potato** | **Stem** (tuber, with "eyes" = buds) |
| **Ginger, turmeric** | **Stem** (rhizome) |
| **Onion** | **Stem (bulb) with fleshy leaves** |
| **Sweet potato, carrot, radish** | **Root** |
| **Cauliflower, broccoli** | **Inflorescence (flower)** |
| **Cabbage, spinach, tea** | **Leaf** |
| **Coconut water** | **Liquid endosperm** |
| Mango, jackfruit, tomato | Fruit (edible part differs; tomato is botanically a fruit) |
| Rice, wheat | Grain (fruit-seed, caryopsis) |

## Reproduction and nutrition
- **Pollination (পরাগায়ন)**: transfer of pollen; by **insects** (colourful, scented flowers), **wind** (rice, maize, grasses), water, birds, animals.
- **Seed germination** needs **water, air (oxygen) and suitable temperature** (light is not essential for most seeds).
- **Nitrogen fixation**: **Rhizobium** bacteria in **root nodules of legumes** (pulses, peas, beans) fix atmospheric nitrogen. Blue-green algae (Anabaena) do this in rice fields.
- Insectivorous plants (pitcher plant, sundew, Venus flytrap) trap insects for **nitrogen**. **Cuscuta (স্বর্ণলতা)** is a **parasite**; lichen is a symbiosis of **alga + fungus**.

## Famous botanists and record plants 🔥
| Fact | Name |
|---|---|
| **Father of botany** | **Theophrastus** |
| **Binomial nomenclature**; father of taxonomy (*Species Plantarum*, 1753) | **Carl Linnaeus** |
| **Plants have life/feelings**; invented the **crescograph** | **Jagadish Chandra Bose** |
| Laws of heredity (pea plants) | Gregor Mendel |
| **Largest flower** | **Rafflesia arnoldii** |
| **Tallest tree** | **Redwood (Sequoia)** |
| **Smallest flowering plant** | **Wolffia** |

> **Why it matters:** Exams ask scientific names (tiger, hilsa, human, mosquitoes), which phylum an animal belongs to, "which of these is not a fish/insect/mammal", heart chambers of vertebrate classes and the five-kingdom system.

## Classification basics 🔥
- **Aristotle** is called the **father of biology and zoology**. **Carl Linnaeus** (Sweden) introduced **binomial nomenclature (দ্বিপদ নামকরণ)** — *Systema Naturae* (1758 edition for animals) — and is the **father of taxonomy**.
- A scientific name has **two parts: genus + species** (genus capitalised, species small, written in italics), e.g. ***Homo sapiens***.
- **Taxonomic hierarchy**: **Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species**. **Species** is the basic unit.
- **Five-kingdom system: R. H. Whittaker (1969)** — **Monera** (bacteria, cyanobacteria), **Protista** (Amoeba, Paramecium, Plasmodium, Euglena), **Fungi**, **Plantae**, **Animalia**.

## Scientific names 🔥🔥
| Common name | Scientific name |
|---|---|
| **Human** | ***Homo sapiens*** |
| **Royal Bengal tiger** (national animal) | ***Panthera tigris*** (subspecies *P. tigris tigris*) |
| Lion | *Panthera leo* |
| **Hilsa (ইলিশ)** (national fish) | ***Tenualosa ilisha*** |
| **Magpie robin (দোয়েল)** (national bird) | ***Copsychus saularis*** |
| Bull frog (কোলাব্যাঙ) | *Hoplobatrachus tigerinus* (older name *Rana tigrina*) |
| Cat | *Felis catus* |
| Dog | *Canis familiaris* (*C. lupus familiaris*) |
| Housefly | *Musca domestica* |
| Honey bee | *Apis* spp. (e.g. *Apis indica/cerana*) |
| Rohu (রুই) | *Labeo rohita* |
| **Mango** | ***Mangifera indica*** |
| **Rice** | ***Oryza sativa*** |
| **Jute** | ***Corchorus capsularis*** (white/deshi), ***C. olitorius*** (tossa) |
| Jackfruit | *Artocarpus heterophyllus* |
| Water lily (শাপলা) | *Nymphaea nouchali* |
| Potato | *Solanum tuberosum* |
| Tea | *Camellia sinensis* |

**Mosquitoes and disease:** ***Anopheles*** (female) → **malaria**; ***Aedes aegypti*** → **dengue, chikungunya, Zika, yellow fever**; ***Culex*** → **filaria (elephantiasis)**, Japanese encephalitis.

## Major animal phyla (invertebrates) 🔥
| Phylum | Key features | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Porifera** | Body full of **pores**; simplest multicellular animals | **Sponges** |
| **Cnidaria (Coelenterata)** | Stinging cells (cnidocytes), one opening | **Hydra, jellyfish, sea anemone, coral** |
| **Platyhelminthes** | **Flatworms**; mostly parasites | **Tapeworm**, liver fluke, planaria |
| **Nematoda** | **Roundworms**; unsegmented | **Ascaris (roundworm), hookworm, filarial worm**, pinworm |
| **Annelida** | **Segmented worms** | **Earthworm** (farmer's friend; breathes through **skin**), **leech** (secretes anticoagulant **hirudin**) |
| **Arthropoda** | **Jointed legs**, chitin exoskeleton; **largest phylum** | Insects, **spiders**, scorpion, **crab, prawn**, centipede |
| **Mollusca** | **Soft body**, usually a shell | **Snail, oyster** (pearl), mussel, **octopus, squid, cuttlefish** |
| **Echinodermata** | **Spiny skin**, water-vascular system, marine only | **Starfish**, sea urchin, sea cucumber |
| **Chordata** | **Notochord**, dorsal nerve cord | Fish, frogs, reptiles, birds, mammals |

- **Insects**: **6 legs, 3 body parts** (head, thorax, abdomen), 1 pair of antennae. **Spiders and scorpions have 8 legs** — they are **arachnids, not insects**.
- **Cockroach** has a 13-chambered heart; its blood is colourless (no haemoglobin).
- **Octopus has 3 hearts**. **Hydra** can regenerate.
- **Coral**: **St. Martin's Island** is Bangladesh's **only coral island**.

## Vertebrate classes (মেরুদণ্ডী প্রাণী) 🔥🔥
| Class | Key features | Heart chambers | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pisces (fish)** | **Gills**, fins, scales; cold-blooded | **2** | Hilsa, rohu, shark, **seahorse** |
| **Amphibia** | Live on land and water; moist skin; larva (**tadpole**) has gills; adult breathes by lungs and **skin**; cold-blooded | **3** | Frog, toad, salamander |
| **Reptilia** | Dry scaly skin, lay shelled eggs; cold-blooded | **3** (**crocodile has 4**) | Snake, lizard, turtle, crocodile |
| **Aves (birds)** | **Feathers**, beak, **hollow bones**, lay eggs; **warm-blooded** | **4** | Magpie robin, pigeon, penguin |
| **Mammalia** | **Hair**, **mammary glands**, external ear, diaphragm; mostly give birth; warm-blooded | **4** | Human, cow, **whale, bat** |

- **Cold-blooded (poikilothermic, শীতল রক্ত)**: fish, amphibians, reptiles. **Warm-blooded (homeothermic)**: **birds and mammals**.

## "Odd one out" facts 🔥
| Animal | Actually is |
|---|---|
| **Prawn/shrimp (চিংড়ি), crab** | **Arthropod**, not fish |
| **Starfish** | Echinoderm, not fish |
| **Jellyfish** | Cnidarian, not fish |
| **Cuttlefish, octopus** | Mollusc, not fish |
| Silverfish | Insect |
| **Seahorse** | **A true fish** |
| **Whale, dolphin** | **Mammals** (breathe with lungs) |
| **Bat** | **Mammal** — the **only flying mammal** |
| **Platypus, echidna** | **Egg-laying mammals** (monotremes, Australia) |
| Kangaroo, koala | Pouched mammals (**marsupials**) |
| Tortoise/turtle | Reptile |
| Penguin, ostrich, emu, kiwi | **Flightless birds** |

## Record animals
- **Largest animal: blue whale**. **Largest land animal: African elephant**. **Largest bird: ostrich**; **smallest bird: hummingbird**. **Fastest land animal: cheetah**. Largest reptile: saltwater crocodile.

## Quick revision
- Linnaeus: **binomial nomenclature**; Whittaker: **five kingdoms (1969)**.
- **Homo sapiens**; tiger *Panthera tigris*; hilsa *Tenualosa ilisha*; doyel *Copsychus saularis*.
- Mango *Mangifera indica*; rice *Oryza sativa*; jute *Corchorus*.
- **Anopheles → malaria; Aedes → dengue; Culex → filaria.**
- **Arthropoda = largest phylum**; insects 6 legs, spiders 8.
- Heart: fish 2, amphibian 3, reptile 3 (crocodile 4), birds & mammals 4.
- **Prawn is an arthropod; whale and bat are mammals; seahorse is a fish.**
- Earthworm breathes through skin; leech makes hirudin.

SCI-17.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask enzymes and where they act, the largest gland, blood cell counts and life span, blood groups (universal donor/recipient), normal blood pressure and heart rate, and who discovered blood circulation.

## Digestive system (পরিপাকতন্ত্র) 🔥
| Part | Juice / enzyme | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **Mouth** | Saliva: **ptyalin (salivary amylase)** | **Starch → maltose**; digestion of starch begins here |
| **Stomach** | Gastric juice: **HCl**, **pepsin**, **rennin** (infants) | HCl kills germs, makes medium acidic (pH ≈ 2); **pepsin: protein → peptides**; rennin curdles milk |
| **Liver** | **Bile** (stored in the **gall bladder**) | **Emulsifies fat**; bile has **no enzyme** |
| **Pancreas** | Pancreatic juice: **amylase, trypsin, lipase** | Starch, protein, fat digestion |
| **Small intestine** | Intestinal juice (maltase, sucrase, lactase, lipase, peptidases) | **Digestion completes**; **most absorption** through **villi** |
| **Large intestine** | — | **Absorbs water**, forms faeces |

- **Liver is the largest gland** (and largest internal organ, ≈ 1.5 kg). It makes bile, stores **glycogen**, iron and vitamins A, D, B₁₂; detoxifies; makes urea. Jaundice is a liver disorder (bilirubin rises).
- **Pancreas is a mixed gland**: exocrine (digestive enzymes) and endocrine (**insulin, glucagon**).
- **Small intestine** is the **longest part** of the alimentary canal (≈ 6–7 m). Whole canal ≈ 9 m.
- Final products: carbohydrate → **glucose**; protein → **amino acids**; fat → **fatty acids + glycerol**.
- **Teeth**: adults **32** (permanent), children **20** (milk teeth). **Enamel** is the **hardest substance in the body**. Largest salivary gland: **parotid** (swells in **mumps**).
- **Appendix** is a vestigial organ attached to the large intestine.

## Blood (রক্ত) 🔥🔥
- Blood is a **fluid connective tissue**. An adult has about **5–6 litres** (≈ 7–8% of body weight). **pH ≈ 7.4** (slightly alkaline).
- **Plasma ≈ 55%** (about 90% water, plus proteins such as albumin, fibrinogen, globulin); **blood cells ≈ 45%**.

| Cell | Normal count (per mm³) | Life span | Main job |
|---|---|---|---|
| **RBC (erythrocyte, লোহিত কণিকা)** | **≈ 4.5–5.5 million** (men ≈ 5 m, women ≈ 4.5 m) | **≈ 120 days** | Carries **O₂** by **haemoglobin (iron-containing)**; **no nucleus** in mammals |
| **WBC (leucocyte, শ্বেত কণিকা)** | **≈ 4,000–11,000** | Hours to days (lymphocytes longer) | **Defence**; lymphocytes make **antibodies**; neutrophils most numerous, eat germs |
| **Platelet (thrombocyte, অণুচক্রিকা)** | **≈ 1.5–4 lakh** | ≈ 7–10 days | **Blood clotting**; count falls in **dengue** |

- RBCs are made in the **red bone marrow** (in the fetus, also liver/spleen). Old RBCs are destroyed in the **spleen** ("graveyard of RBC").
- **Haemoglobin**: men ≈ 13–17 g/dL, women ≈ 12–15 g/dL (values vary slightly between books). Low haemoglobin/RBC = **anaemia (রক্তস্বল্পতা)**. Uncontrolled WBC increase = **leukaemia (blood cancer)**.
- **Clotting** needs **vitamin K**, **calcium**, fibrinogen → fibrin; usually 3–8 minutes. **Haemophilia** ("bleeder's disease") is a hereditary, **X-linked** disorder in which blood does not clot.
- **Heparin** (from liver) prevents clotting inside vessels.

## Blood groups 🔥🔥
- **ABO blood groups** discovered by **Karl Landsteiner (1900–01)** (Nobel 1930). **Rh factor**: Landsteiner & Wiener (**1940**), named after the **rhesus monkey**.

| Group | Antigen on RBC | Antibody in plasma | Can receive from |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | A | anti-B | A, O |
| B | B | anti-A | B, O |
| **AB** | A and B | **none** | **All → universal recipient** |
| **O** | **none** | anti-A and anti-B | O only → **universal donor** |

- **O negative (O−)** is the true universal donor; **AB positive** the universal recipient.
- **Rh incompatibility**: an **Rh− mother** carrying an **Rh+ baby** can cause **erythroblastosis fetalis** in later pregnancies.
- A healthy adult can donate blood about **every 4 months**.

## Heart and circulation (হৃৎপিণ্ড ও রক্ত সংবহন) 🔥
- **Blood circulation** was discovered by **William Harvey (1628)**. **Capillaries** were discovered by **Marcello Malpighi**.
- Human heart has **4 chambers**: 2 **atria (অলিন্দ)** and 2 **ventricles (নিলয়)**. Right side carries **deoxygenated**, left side **oxygenated** blood. The **left ventricle** has the thickest wall (pumps to the whole body).
- The heart's natural **pacemaker** is the **SA (sinoatrial) node**. Heart weighs about **300 g**; covered by the **pericardium**.
- **Normal heart rate ≈ 72 beats/min** (range 60–100); one cardiac cycle ≈ **0.8 s**. Heart sounds: "lub-dub" (valve closure).
- **Normal blood pressure ≈ 120/80 mmHg** (systolic/diastolic); **140/90 or more = hypertension**. Measured with a **sphygmomanometer**.

| Vessel | Carries | Exception |
|---|---|---|
| **Artery (ধমনী)** | Blood **away from** the heart; oxygenated | **Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated** blood (to lungs) |
| **Vein (শিরা)** | Blood **to** the heart; deoxygenated; has valves | **Pulmonary vein carries oxygenated** blood (from lungs) |
| **Capillary** | Exchange between blood and tissues | — |

- **Aorta** is the **largest artery**; **vena cava** the **largest vein**.
- **Double circulation**: pulmonary (heart → lungs → heart) and systemic (heart → body → heart).
- **First human heart transplant: Christiaan Barnard, 1967, South Africa**.
- **Lymph** is a colourless fluid; lymph nodes filter germs.

## Quick revision
- Starch digestion starts in the **mouth (ptyalin)**; protein in the **stomach (pepsin)**.
- **Bile** from the liver emulsifies fat, has no enzyme; **liver = largest gland**.
- Digestion completes and absorption happens in the **small intestine**.
- **RBC life 120 days**; made in bone marrow; destroyed in spleen.
- Platelets help clotting; vitamin K needed; haemophilia = no clotting.
- **O = universal donor, AB = universal recipient**; Landsteiner discovered ABO.
- **BP 120/80 mmHg; heart rate 72/min**; pacemaker = SA node.
- **Harvey (1628)** discovered circulation; pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood.

SCI-18.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask which part of the brain controls balance/heartbeat, functional unit of kidney, breathing rate, the "master gland", which hormone controls blood sugar or causes goitre, and bone counts.

## Nervous system (স্নায়ুতন্ত্র) 🔥
- The **neuron** is the structural and functional unit; the **longest cell** of the body. A junction between neurons is a **synapse**; a common chemical messenger is **acetylcholine**.
- Adult brain weighs about **1.3–1.4 kg**; protected by the skull and meninges; cerebrospinal fluid cushions it.

| Part of brain | Main function |
|---|---|
| **Cerebrum (গুরুমস্তিষ্ক)** | **Largest part**; **intelligence, memory, thinking, will, speech**, senses |
| **Cerebellum (লঘুমস্তিষ্ক)** | **Balance (ভারসাম্য)** and **coordination** of muscles; affected by alcohol |
| **Medulla oblongata (সুষুম্নাশীর্ষক)** | **Involuntary actions**: **heartbeat, breathing**, swallowing, coughing, vomiting |
| **Hypothalamus** | **Body temperature**, hunger, thirst; controls the pituitary |
| **Spinal cord (সুষুম্নাকাণ্ড)** | **Reflex actions** (e.g. pulling hand from a hot object), message pathway |

- **12 pairs of cranial nerves** and **31 pairs of spinal nerves**.
- **Reflex action** is quick and automatic, controlled mainly by the **spinal cord**.
- **Senses**: eye (retina — rods & cones), ear (**cochlea → hearing**; **semicircular canals → balance**), nose, tongue, skin. **Skin is the largest organ**.
- Skeleton: an **adult has 206 bones** (a newborn has about 300, which fuse). **Longest bone: femur (thigh)**; **smallest: stapes (ear)**.

## Respiratory system (শ্বসনতন্ত্র) 🔥
- Air path: **nose → pharynx → larynx (voice box, "Adam's apple") → trachea (windpipe) → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli**.
- **Alveoli (বায়ুথলি)** are the site of **gas exchange** by diffusion; about **30 crore (300 million)** in the two lungs.
- **Epiglottis** closes the windpipe while swallowing. **Right lung has 3 lobes, left lung 2** (space for the heart).
- **Diaphragm** is the main breathing muscle; it contracts (flattens) during inhalation.
- **Normal breathing rate of an adult: ≈ 12–20 times per minute** (many books: 16–20); higher in infants.
- Tidal volume ≈ **500 mL**; vital capacity ≈ 4–5 L.

| Gas | Inhaled air | Exhaled air |
|---|---|---|
| **Oxygen** | **≈ 21%** | ≈ 16% |
| **Carbon dioxide** | **≈ 0.04%** | **≈ 4%** |
| Nitrogen | ≈ 78% | ≈ 78% |

- O₂ is carried mainly by **haemoglobin** (as oxyhaemoglobin); CO₂ mostly as **bicarbonate** in plasma.
- **Cellular respiration** occurs in **mitochondria**; anaerobic respiration in muscle makes **lactic acid** (causes fatigue/cramps).

## Excretory system (রেচনতন্ত্র) 🔥
- **Kidneys (বৃক্ক)**: bean-shaped, ≈ 150 g each. **Functional unit: nephron** — about **10 lakh (1 million)** per kidney. Parts: **glomerulus** and **Bowman's capsule** (filtration), tubules (reabsorption).
- **Urea** is made in the **liver** and removed by the kidneys. It is the main nitrogenous waste in humans.
- Adults pass about **1–1.5 litres of urine per day** (≈ 95% water). Yellow colour: **urochrome**.
- **Kidney stones** are mostly **calcium oxalate**. Kidney failure is treated by **dialysis** or transplant (first successful kidney transplant: **1954, Joseph Murray**, USA).
- Other excretory organs: **lungs (CO₂), skin (sweat), liver (bile pigments)**.
- **ADH (vasopressin)** makes kidneys reabsorb water; lack of ADH → **diabetes insipidus** (lots of dilute urine).

## Hormones and endocrine glands (হরমোন ও অন্তঃক্ষরা গ্রন্থি) 🔥🔥
- Endocrine glands are **ductless**; they release **hormones** directly into the **blood**. The word "hormone" was used by **Bayliss and Starling (1905)**; the first hormone discovered was **secretin**.

| Gland | Hormone | Job / disorder |
|---|---|---|
| **Pituitary (পিটুইটারি)** | Growth hormone, TSH, ACTH, **ADH**, **oxytocin**, prolactin | **"Master gland"** — controls other glands; pea-sized, at the base of the brain. Excess GH → **gigantism** (child) / acromegaly (adult); lack → **dwarfism**. **Oxytocin** → childbirth contractions, milk ejection |
| **Thyroid (থাইরয়েড)** | **Thyroxine** (contains **iodine**) | Controls **metabolism**; **largest endocrine gland**. **Iodine lack → goitre (গলগণ্ড)**; lack in children → **cretinism**; in adults → myxoedema; excess → hyperthyroidism (**Graves' disease**, bulging eyes) |
| **Parathyroid** | **Parathormone** | **Calcium** and phosphate balance in blood |
| **Adrenal (অ্যাড্রিনাল)** | **Adrenaline** (medulla), cortisol, aldosterone (cortex) | Adrenaline = **"emergency / fight-or-flight hormone"**: raises heartbeat, BP, blood sugar |
| **Pancreas — islets of Langerhans** | **Insulin** (β-cells), **glucagon** (α-cells) | **Insulin lowers blood sugar**; its lack → **diabetes mellitus**. Glucagon raises blood sugar |
| **Testis** | **Testosterone** | Male characteristics |
| **Ovary** | **Oestrogen, progesterone** | Female characteristics; progesterone maintains **pregnancy** |
| **Pineal** | **Melatonin** | **Sleep–wake cycle** (biological clock) |
| **Thymus** | Thymosin | Immunity (T-cells) in childhood |

- **Insulin** was discovered by **Frederick Banting and Charles Best (1921)**; Banting shared the Nobel Prize in 1923.
- **Normal fasting blood glucose ≈ 3.9–5.5 mmol/L (70–100 mg/dL)**; **fasting ≥ 7.0 mmol/L** indicates diabetes (WHO).
- **Pancreas is a mixed gland** (both exocrine and endocrine).

## Quick revision
- **Cerebellum = balance**; **medulla = heartbeat & breathing**; **cerebrum = intelligence/memory**.
- Reflex action: **spinal cord**; 12 pairs cranial, 31 pairs spinal nerves.
- **206 bones**; femur longest, stapes smallest; skin largest organ.
- Gas exchange in **alveoli**; breathing ≈ 12–20/min; exhaled CO₂ ≈ 4%.
- **Nephron = unit of kidney**; urea made in liver; kidney stone = calcium oxalate.
- **Pituitary = master gland**; **thyroxine needs iodine** (goitre).
- **Insulin lowers blood sugar** (Banting & Best, 1921); **adrenaline = emergency hormone**.
- Melatonin: sleep; oxytocin: childbirth and milk ejection.

SCI-19.notes:
> **Why it matters:** "Lack of which vitamin causes night blindness / scurvy / rickets / beriberi?" and "which mineral prevents goitre / anaemia?" are asked in almost every job exam. Learn the tables below by heart.

## Vitamins: basics 🔥
- The word "vitamine" was coined by **Casimir Funk (1912)**. Vitamins are needed in small amounts and give **no energy (calories)**.
- **Fat-soluble: A, D, E, K** (stored in the body, mainly liver). **Water-soluble: B-complex and C** (not stored much; excess passes in urine; B₁₂ is an exception, stored in liver).
- **Vitamin C** is the vitamin **most easily destroyed by heat/cooking** and air.
- Vitamins the body can make: **D (in skin, from sunlight)** and **K (by intestinal bacteria)**.

## Vitamin deficiency table 🔥🔥🔥
| Vitamin (chemical name) | Deficiency disease / symptom | Good sources |
|---|---|---|
| **A (retinol)** | **Night blindness (রাতকানা)**, **xerophthalmia** (dry eye), skin problems | **Carrot, ripe mango, pumpkin, green leafy vegetables**, liver, **fish-liver oil**, egg yolk, milk, **mola fish (মলা মাছ)**; plants give **β-carotene (provitamin A)** |
| **B₁ (thiamine)** | **Beriberi (বেরিবেরি)** — nerve and heart problems | Whole grains, **husk of rice (unpolished/ঢেঁকিছাটা rice)**, pulses, yeast |
| **B₂ (riboflavin)** | **Cracks at the corners of the mouth, sore tongue and lips (angular stomatitis / ariboflavinosis, মুখে ঘা)** | Milk, egg, liver, green vegetables |
| **B₃ (niacin / nicotinic acid)** | **Pellagra** — the "4 Ds": dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia, death | Meat, fish, groundnut, whole grains |
| B₅ (pantothenic acid) | Rare (burning feet) | Widely present |
| **B₆ (pyridoxine)** | Anaemia, skin problems, convulsions | Meat, fish, grains |
| B₇ (biotin) | Skin/hair problems (rare) | Egg yolk, liver |
| **B₉ (folic acid)** | **Megaloblastic anaemia**; **birth defects (neural tube)** in pregnancy | Green leafy vegetables, liver, pulses |
| **B₁₂ (cyanocobalamin)** — contains **cobalt** | **Pernicious anaemia**, nerve damage | **Only animal foods**: meat, fish, egg, milk, liver |
| **C (ascorbic acid)** | **Scurvy (স্কার্ভি)** — **bleeding and swollen gums**, slow wound healing | **Amla (আমলকী)** (very rich), **guava**, lemon, orange, green chilli, tomato |
| **D (calciferol)** | **Rickets (রিকেটস)** in children (bent legs); **osteomalacia** in adults | **Sunlight** ("**sunshine vitamin**"), **fish-liver oil**, egg yolk, milk |
| **E (tocopherol)** | **Infertility / reproductive problems**, muscle weakness | Vegetable oils, nuts, green leaves; an **antioxidant**; called the "**anti-sterility vitamin**" |
| **K (phylloquinone)** | **Delayed blood clotting**, bleeding (haemorrhage) | Green leafy vegetables; made by **gut bacteria**; newborns often given a vitamin K injection |

**Memory hooks:**
- *A for eyes (রাতকানা); B₁ Beriberi; C for gums (scurvy); D for bones (rickets); K for Klotting.*
- **James Lind (1747)** showed that citrus fruit (lemon) prevents scurvy in sailors.
- Bangladesh runs a national **Vitamin A capsule** campaign for children (6–59 months) to prevent night blindness.

## Minerals (খনিজ লবণ) 🔥🔥
| Mineral | Role | Deficiency | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Calcium (Ca)** | **Bones and teeth**, blood clotting, muscle action | **Rickets, osteoporosis** (weak bones), tooth decay | **Milk**, small fish with bones, green vegetables |
| **Iron (Fe)** | Part of **haemoglobin** (O₂ transport) | **Anaemia (রক্তস্বল্পতা)** | Liver, meat, **spinach, kochu shak (কচু শাক)**, pulses, jaggery |
| **Iodine (I)** | Makes **thyroxine** | **Goitre (গলগণ্ড)**; **cretinism** in children | **Iodised salt**, sea fish, seaweed |
| Phosphorus (P) | Bones, teeth, **ATP**, DNA | Weak bones | Milk, meat, grains |
| **Sodium (Na)** | Fluid balance, nerve impulses | Muscle cramps, low BP (e.g. after diarrhoea/sweating) | Common salt |
| **Potassium (K)** | Nerve, muscle and **heart** function | Muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat | Banana, potato, coconut water |
| **Fluorine (F)** | Hardens tooth enamel | **Dental caries**; excess → **fluorosis** (mottled teeth) | Fluoridated water, toothpaste |
| **Zinc (Zn)** | Growth, immunity, wound healing | Stunted growth; **zinc is given with ORS in diarrhoea** | Meat, seafood, pulses |
| Magnesium (Mg) | Enzymes, muscles | Muscle cramps | Green vegetables, nuts |
| Cobalt (Co) | Part of **vitamin B₁₂** | Anaemia | Animal foods |

## Protein and energy deficiency 🔥
| Disease | Cause | Signs |
|---|---|---|
| **Kwashiorkor** | Mainly **protein** deficiency | Swollen belly and legs (**oedema**), skin/hair changes |
| **Marasmus** | **Protein + calorie (energy)** deficiency | Extreme thinness, "skin and bones" |

- Energy per gram: **carbohydrate ≈ 4 kcal, protein ≈ 4 kcal, fat ≈ 9 kcal** (fat gives the most energy).
- **Soybean** is a very rich plant protein source (≈ 40% protein). Six food groups: carbohydrate, protein, fat, vitamins, minerals, **water** (≈ 60–70% of body weight).
- A **balanced diet (সুষম খাদ্য)** contains all six in proper proportion.

## Quick revision
- **A → night blindness; B₁ → beriberi; B₃ → pellagra; C → scurvy; D → rickets; K → poor clotting.**
- **B₁₂ contains cobalt**, found only in animal foods; lack → pernicious anaemia.
- Folic acid lack → anaemia and birth defects.
- **Fat-soluble: A, D, E, K**; vitamin C is destroyed by cooking.
- **Sunshine vitamin = D**; amla and guava are rich in **vitamin C**.
- **Iron → anaemia; iodine → goitre; calcium → bones; fluorine → tooth decay.**
- **Kwashiorkor = protein lack; marasmus = protein + energy lack.**
- Fat gives 9 kcal/g, the highest.

SCI-20.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask "which disease is caused by a virus/bacterium/protozoan?", carriers (vectors), who discovered which germ or vaccine, what BCG protects against, and Bangladesh's EPI and disease-elimination milestones.

## Disease by pathogen type 🔥🔥🔥
| Pathogen | Diseases |
|---|---|
| **Virus (ভাইরাস)** | **COVID-19**, influenza (flu), **common cold**, **dengue**, **chikungunya**, Zika, yellow fever, **polio**, **measles (হাম)**, **mumps**, rubella, **chickenpox**, **smallpox**, **rabies (জলাতঙ্ক)**, **hepatitis A, B, C, E (জন্ডিস)**, **HIV/AIDS**, **Nipah**, Ebola, bird flu (H5N1), swine flu (H1N1), herpes, mpox |
| **Bacterium (ব্যাকটেরিয়া)** | **Tuberculosis (যক্ষ্মা)**, **cholera (কলেরা)**, **typhoid**, **diphtheria**, **whooping cough (pertussis)**, **tetanus (ধনুষ্টংকার)**, **leprosy (কুষ্ঠ)**, **plague**, **anthrax**, bacterial pneumonia, **bacillary dysentery** (Shigella), syphilis, gonorrhoea, botulism |
| **Protozoa (প্রোটোজোয়া)** | **Malaria** (*Plasmodium*), **kala-azar** (*Leishmania donovani*), **amoebic dysentery** (*Entamoeba histolytica*), sleeping sickness (*Trypanosoma*) |
| **Fungus (ছত্রাক)** | **Ringworm (দাদ)**, athlete's foot, dandruff, candidiasis (note: **scabies** is caused by a **mite**, not a fungus) |
| **Worms (কৃমি)** | **Filaria / elephantiasis (গোদ)** (*Wuchereria bancrofti*), roundworm (*Ascaris*), hookworm, tapeworm |

- **Antibiotics kill bacteria, not viruses.**
- **Jaundice** is a symptom (high bilirubin), most often from viral **hepatitis**. **Hepatitis B and C** spread through **blood** and can cause liver cancer; **A and E** spread through contaminated food/water.
- **Pneumonia** can be bacterial or viral.

## Carriers (vectors) 🔥
| Carrier | Disease |
|---|---|
| **Female *Anopheles* mosquito** | **Malaria** |
| ***Aedes aegypti*** (and *Ae. albopictus*) | **Dengue, chikungunya**, Zika, yellow fever |
| ***Culex*** mosquito | **Filaria**, Japanese encephalitis |
| **Sandfly** | **Kala-azar** |
| **Housefly** | Cholera, typhoid, dysentery (carries germs mechanically) |
| **Rat flea** | **Plague** |
| **Dog (bite)**, cat, jackal, fox | **Rabies** |
| **Fruit bat** (via raw date-palm juice, খেজুরের কাঁচা রস) | **Nipah virus** (first Bangladesh outbreak: **Meherpur, 2001**) |
| Tsetse fly | Sleeping sickness |

## Discoverers of germs, vaccines and drugs 🔥🔥
| Discovery | Person / year |
|---|---|
| **Smallpox vaccine** (from cowpox) — **father of immunology** | **Edward Jenner (1796)** |
| **Rabies vaccine** (1885), anthrax vaccine, **pasteurisation**, germ theory | **Louis Pasteur** |
| **TB bacterium** (1882), cholera bacterium (1883) | **Robert Koch** |
| Malaria parasite in blood (1880) | Alphonse Laveran |
| **Mosquito transmits malaria** (1897) | **Ronald Ross** (Nobel 1902) |
| Leprosy bacterium | Gerhard Armauer Hansen |
| **Penicillin — first antibiotic (1928)** | **Alexander Fleming** |
| Streptomycin (first effective TB antibiotic) | Selman Waksman |
| **Injectable polio vaccine (IPV, 1955)** | **Jonas Salk** |
| **Oral polio vaccine (OPV)** | **Albert Sabin** |
| **BCG vaccine** (against TB, 1921) | **Calmette & Guérin** |
| **HIV** identified (1983) | Luc Montagnier & Françoise Barré-Sinoussi |
| Artemisinin for malaria (Nobel 2015) | Tu Youyou |
| Quinine (old malaria drug) | From **cinchona** bark |

- **BCG = Bacillus Calmette–Guérin**, given at birth **against tuberculosis**.
- **Smallpox** is the **only human disease eradicated** worldwide — WHO declared it in **1980**.
- **ORS (oral saline)** treats dehydration from **diarrhoea/cholera**; **icddr,b (Dhaka)** played a key role in developing and proving it. Zinc is given with ORS.

## Bangladesh: EPI and milestones 🔥
- **EPI (Expanded Programme on Immunization)** in Bangladesh started on **7 April 1979**; it expanded nationwide from **1985**.
- Main EPI vaccines: **BCG** (TB), **Pentavalent** (**diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B, Hib**), **OPV and IPV** (polio), **PCV** (pneumococcal pneumonia), **MR** (measles-rubella), and **TT/Td** for women. **HPV vaccine** (against cervical cancer) for girls was introduced in **2023**; a nationwide **typhoid conjugate vaccine** campaign followed later.
- Bangladesh was **certified polio-free in March 2014** (with the WHO South-East Asia Region).
- WHO validated Bangladesh's elimination of **lymphatic filariasis (2023)** and of **kala-azar** as a public-health problem (**October 2023**, the **first country** to be validated for kala-azar).

> 🔄 Update: check the latest EPI schedule and new vaccine campaigns in a newspaper or the DGHS website.

## COVID-19 and other key facts
- **COVID-19** is caused by **SARS-CoV-2** (a coronavirus); first reported in **Wuhan, China (December 2019)**; WHO declared a **pandemic on 11 March 2020**. Bangladesh reported its first cases on **8 March 2020**. WHO ended the global health emergency on **5 May 2023**.
- **Dengue**: no specific antiviral drug; **platelet count falls**; early test **NS1 antigen**. Aedes breeds in **clean, stagnant water**.
- **Rabies** is almost always fatal once symptoms appear; post-bite vaccination is essential. Also called **hydrophobia** (fear of water).
- **Tetanus** causes "lockjaw"; spores in soil/rust enter through wounds.
- Important days: **World TB Day 24 March**, **World Malaria Day 25 April**, **World AIDS Day 1 December**, World Health Day 7 April (WHO founded 1948, HQ **Geneva**).

## Quick revision
- **Virus**: COVID-19, dengue, polio, measles, rabies, hepatitis, AIDS, Nipah, chickenpox.
- **Bacteria**: TB, cholera, typhoid, diphtheria, tetanus, leprosy, plague, whooping cough.
- **Protozoa**: malaria, kala-azar, amoebic dysentery. **Fungus**: ringworm.
- **Anopheles → malaria; Aedes → dengue; Culex → filaria; sandfly → kala-azar.**
- **Jenner: smallpox vaccine (1796); Pasteur: rabies vaccine; Koch: TB germ; Fleming: penicillin (1928).**
- **Salk: IPV; Sabin: OPV; BCG protects against TB.**
- Smallpox eradicated **1980**; Bangladesh polio-free **2014**; EPI began **1979**.

SCI-21.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the father of genetics, DNA structure and its discoverers, human chromosome number and sex determination, genetic disorders, and biotechnology milestones (Dolly, Bt brinjal, jute genome, DNA fingerprinting, CRISPR).

## Mendel and heredity (বংশগতি) 🔥
- **Gregor Johann Mendel** (Austrian monk) is the **father of genetics**. He experimented on **pea plants (মটরশুঁটি)** and published in **1866**; his work was rediscovered in **1900** (de Vries, Correns, Tschermak).
- **Laws**: (1) **Law of segregation**, (2) **Law of independent assortment**. Dominant and recessive traits.
- **Monohybrid cross (F₂)**: phenotype ratio **3 : 1**, genotype ratio **1 : 2 : 1**. **Dihybrid cross (F₂)**: **9 : 3 : 3 : 1**.
- Term **"genetics"**: **William Bateson (1905)**. Term **"gene"**: **Wilhelm Johannsen (1909)**. **Mutation** theory: **Hugo de Vries**. Chromosome theory of inheritance: Sutton & Boveri; **T. H. Morgan** (fruit fly) showed genes lie on chromosomes.

## Chromosomes and sex determination 🔥
- **Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs)**: **22 pairs autosomes + 1 pair sex chromosomes**. Gametes (sperm/egg) have 23.
- **Female = XX; male = XY**. The mother always gives X; the **father's sperm (X or Y) decides the sex of the child**.
- A **gene** is a segment of DNA on a chromosome that codes for a trait/protein.

| Genetic disorder | Cause |
|---|---|
| **Down syndrome** | **Extra chromosome 21 (trisomy 21)** → 47 chromosomes |
| **Turner syndrome** | Female with only one X (**XO**, 45) |
| **Klinefelter syndrome** | Male with **XXY** (47) |
| **Haemophilia** (blood doesn't clot) | **X-linked recessive** → mostly in **males** |
| **Colour blindness** (red-green) | **X-linked recessive** → mostly in males |
| **Thalassaemia** | Inherited haemoglobin disorder (autosomal recessive); **common in Bangladesh**; needs regular blood transfusion |
| Sickle-cell anaemia | Abnormal haemoglobin; sickle-shaped RBCs |

## DNA and RNA 🔥🔥
- DNA (**deoxyribonucleic acid**) is the **hereditary material**. It was first isolated as "nuclein" by **Friedrich Miescher (1869)**.
- **Double-helix model: James Watson & Francis Crick (1953)**, using X-ray images by **Rosalind Franklin** and Maurice Wilkins. Watson, Crick and Wilkins got the **Nobel Prize in 1962**.
- A **nucleotide** = sugar + phosphate + nitrogen base.

| | DNA | RNA |
|---|---|---|
| Sugar | **Deoxyribose** | **Ribose** |
| Bases | **A, T, G, C** | **A, U, G, C** (**uracil instead of thymine**) |
| Strands | **Double** | Usually single |
| Location | Mainly **nucleus** (also mitochondria, chloroplast) | Nucleus and cytoplasm |

- **Base pairing: A = T (2 hydrogen bonds), G ≡ C (3 hydrogen bonds)**.
- Flow of information ("central dogma"): **DNA → RNA → protein** (replication, transcription, translation).
- **Human Genome Project (1990–2003)**: human DNA has ≈ **3 billion base pairs** and about **20,000–25,000 genes**.
- Some viruses (e.g. HIV, SARS-CoV-2) have **RNA** as their genetic material.

## Evolution
- **Charles Darwin**: ***On the Origin of Species* (1859)** — **natural selection** ("survival of the fittest", phrase by Herbert Spencer). Voyage on HMS *Beagle*; Galápagos finches.
- **Lamarck**: **inheritance of acquired characters** (use and disuse; giraffe's neck example).

## Biotechnology (জৈবপ্রযুক্তি) 🔥🔥
- Term "biotechnology": **Karl Ereky (1919)**. **Genetic engineering / recombinant DNA** began in **1972–73** (**Paul Berg**; **Cohen & Boyer**).
- Tools: **restriction enzyme = "molecular scissors"**; **DNA ligase = "molecular glue"**; **plasmid** (circular bacterial DNA) as a **vector**; ***E. coli*** as the common host.

| Milestone | Fact |
|---|---|
| **Human insulin from GM bacteria** | First recombinant drug, marketed **1982** (Humulin) |
| **Dolly the sheep** — first mammal **cloned** from an adult cell | Born **1996** (announced 1997), **Ian Wilmut**, Roslin Institute, **Scotland** |
| **DNA fingerprinting** | **Alec Jeffreys (1984)**; used in **crime investigation and paternity tests** |
| **PCR** (copies DNA millions of times) | **Kary Mullis (1983)** |
| **CRISPR-Cas9** gene editing | **Jennifer Doudna & Emmanuelle Charpentier** — Nobel Chemistry **2020** |
| **First test-tube (IVF) baby** | **Louise Brown, 1978, UK** (Robert Edwards) |
| **Bt crops** | Carry a gene from the bacterium ***Bacillus thuringiensis*** → make their own insecticide (Bt cotton, **Bt brinjal**) |
| **Golden Rice** | Rice engineered to make **β-carotene (provitamin A)** |

## Bangladesh in biotechnology 🔥
- **Bt brinjal (বিটি বেগুন)**: approved in **2013** and released to farmers in **2014** — the **first GM food crop in South Asia**.
- **Jute genome**: a team led by Bangladeshi scientist **Dr. Maqsudul Alam** decoded the **tossa jute genome (announced 2010)**, and later the genome of the jute-attacking fungus ***Macrophomina phaseolina*** (2012) and white jute. He had earlier decoded the **papaya** genome.
- **Tissue culture** is widely used to produce disease-free plantlets (banana, potato, orchids).

## Quick revision
- **Mendel = father of genetics** (pea plant); F₂ ratios **3:1** and **9:3:3:1**.
- Humans: **46 chromosomes**; **XX female, XY male**; father determines sex.
- **Down syndrome = trisomy 21**; haemophilia & colour blindness are **X-linked**.
- **Watson & Crick (1953)**: double helix; Rosalind Franklin's X-ray photo.
- **DNA has thymine; RNA has uracil**; A–T, G–C.
- **Dolly (1996)**: first cloned mammal; **DNA fingerprinting**: Alec Jeffreys.
- **Restriction enzyme = molecular scissors**; plasmid = vector.
- **Bt brinjal (2013)**; **jute genome**: Maqsudul Alam (2010).

SCI-22.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask types of sugars (milk sugar, fruit sugar), which chemical is in tea/chilli/turmeric, pasteurisation and its inventor, food preservatives (sodium benzoate, KMS), harmful adulterants (formalin, calcium carbide) and Bangladesh food-safety laws.

## Nutrients and food chemistry 🔥
**Six food components**: carbohydrate, protein, fat, vitamins, minerals, water. Energy: **carbohydrate ≈ 4 kcal/g, protein ≈ 4 kcal/g, fat ≈ 9 kcal/g**.

| Carbohydrate | Type | Found in |
|---|---|---|
| **Glucose** (grape sugar) | Monosaccharide | Fruits, blood sugar |
| **Fructose (fruit sugar)** | Monosaccharide | Fruits, **honey**; **sweetest natural sugar** |
| Galactose | Monosaccharide | Part of lactose |
| **Sucrose (cane sugar)** | Disaccharide (glucose + fructose) | **Sugarcane, beet** — table sugar |
| **Lactose (milk sugar)** | Disaccharide (glucose + galactose) | **Milk** |
| **Maltose (malt sugar)** | Disaccharide (glucose + glucose) | Germinating grain |
| **Starch** | Polysaccharide | Rice, wheat, potato |
| **Cellulose** | Polysaccharide | Plant cell walls; **humans cannot digest it** — acts as **roughage (fibre)**, prevents constipation |
| **Glycogen ("animal starch")** | Polysaccharide | Stored in **liver and muscles** |

- **Proteins** are made of **amino acids** (about **20** kinds; **9 are essential** for adults and must come from food). Animal proteins (meat, fish, egg, milk) are "**first-class**" (complete) proteins. **Pulses (ডাল)** are called the "**poor man's meat**". Soybean ≈ 40% protein.
- Important food proteins: **casein (milk)**, **albumin (egg white)**, **gluten (wheat)**, **myosin (muscle)**.
- **Fats**: saturated fats (ghee, butter, animal fat) are solid at room temperature; unsaturated fats (soybean, mustard, sunflower oil) are liquid. **Hydrogenation** of vegetable oil with a **nickel catalyst** makes **vanaspati (Dalda)**, which may contain harmful **trans fat**.
- **Milk** is nearly complete food but is **poor in iron and vitamin C**. Honey mainly contains fructose and glucose.

## Chemicals in everyday foods 🔥🔥
| Food | Key compound |
|---|---|
| **Tea** | **Caffeine (theine)**, **tannin** (flavour/astringency) |
| **Coffee** | **Caffeine** |
| **Tobacco** | **Nicotine** |
| Betel nut (সুপারি) | **Arecoline** |
| **Chilli** (hot taste) | **Capsaicin** |
| **Turmeric** (yellow colour) | **Curcumin** |
| **Tomato** (red colour) | **Lycopene** |
| **Carrot** | **Carotene (β-carotene)** |
| Garlic | **Allicin** |
| Onion (tear-causing) | Sulphur compounds (syn-propanethial-S-oxide) |
| Cocoa / chocolate | Theobromine |
| Opium poppy | Morphine |

## Food tests
- **Starch + iodine → blue-black**. **Glucose (reducing sugar) + Benedict's solution (heated) → brick-red**. **Protein + biuret reagent → violet/purple**. Fat leaves a **translucent spot** on paper.

## Microbes in food
- **Fermentation**: **yeast** converts sugar into **alcohol + CO₂** (bread rises, wine/beer). **Lactobacillus** (lactic acid bacteria) turns **milk into curd (দই)/yoghurt**. **Acetobacter** makes **vinegar**. Cheese uses rennet and bacteria.
- **Spoilage** is caused by bacteria, moulds (fungi) and yeast, plus enzymes and oxidation.
- **Aflatoxin**, a cancer-causing toxin, is made by the mould ***Aspergillus flavus*** on damp **groundnuts** and grains. **Botulism** (*Clostridium botulinum*) comes from badly canned food.

## Food preservation methods 🔥🔥
| Method | Principle / example |
|---|---|
| **Drying / dehydration** | Removes water microbes need — dried fish (শুঁটকি), rice, pulses, milk powder |
| **Salting** | Salt draws water out (osmosis) — salted hilsa, pickles |
| **Sugaring** | High sugar (osmosis) — **jam, jelly**, murabba |
| **Pickling** | **Vinegar (acetic acid)** or oil — আচার |
| **Refrigeration / freezing** | **Low temperature slows** microbial growth (fridge ≈ 4 °C; freezer ≈ −18 °C) |
| **Canning** | Heat-sterilised, airtight container — **Nicolas Appert** (France, early 1800s), "father of canning" |
| **Pasteurisation** | **Louis Pasteur** (1860s). Milk heated to **≈ 63 °C for 30 min** or **72 °C for 15 s**, then cooled quickly. **Kills harmful germs** without boiling |
| **UHT** | **≈ 135–140 °C for 2–5 seconds** → long shelf life without refrigeration |
| **Smoking** | Smoke dries and adds antimicrobial compounds — fish, meat |
| **Irradiation** | **Gamma rays (cobalt-60)** kill microbes and insects; stops sprouting of potato/onion |
| **Vacuum packing / freeze drying** | Removes oxygen / water |
| **Chemical preservatives** | See table below |

| Permitted preservative | Used in |
|---|---|
| **Sodium benzoate** | **Acidic foods**: fruit juices, sauces, ketchup, soft drinks |
| **Potassium metabisulphite (KMS)** | **Squashes, fruit juices**, wine (releases SO₂) |
| Sorbic acid / potassium sorbate | Cheese, bakery items |
| Citric acid, vinegar, salt, sugar | Natural preservatives |

## Harmful adulterants (Bangladesh context) 🔥
| Chemical | Illegal misuse | Harm |
|---|---|---|
| **Formalin** (formaldehyde) | To keep **fish, fruit, milk** "fresh" | Cancer, liver/kidney damage |
| **Calcium carbide** | **Artificial ripening** of mango, banana (gives acetylene) | Contains arsenic/phosphorus traces; nerve damage |
| **DDT / insecticides** | On **dried fish** | Toxic, cancer |
| **Textile dyes** | Colouring sweets, spices | Cancer, liver damage |
| **Urea / hydros** | Whitening **puffed rice (মুড়ি)** | Kidney damage |

- **Safe Food Act, 2013 (নিরাপদ খাদ্য আইন)**; under it the **Bangladesh Food Safety Authority (BFSA)** was set up (functional from **2015**).
- **BSTI** (Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution) sets product standards and certification marks.
- **Artificial sweeteners**: saccharin (hundreds of times sweeter than sugar), aspartame, sucralose. **MSG (tasting salt)** is a flavour enhancer.
- **BMI** = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)²; normal **18.5–24.9**; 25–29.9 overweight; 30+ obese.

## Quick revision
- **Milk sugar = lactose; fruit sugar = fructose; cane sugar = sucrose**; animal starch = glycogen.
- Humans can't digest **cellulose** (roughage).
- **Tea: caffeine + tannin; chilli: capsaicin; turmeric: curcumin; tomato: lycopene.**
- **Pasteurisation (Pasteur)**: 63 °C/30 min or 72 °C/15 s; **UHT** ≈ 135–140 °C for seconds.
- **Canning: Nicolas Appert.**
- **Sodium benzoate** and **KMS** are permitted preservatives.
- **Formalin** (fish, fruit) and **calcium carbide** (ripening) are illegal adulterants.
- Curd: **Lactobacillus**; bread/alcohol: **yeast**; aflatoxin: *Aspergillus flavus*.
- **Safe Food Act 2013; BFSA 2015.**

SCI-23.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the main greenhouse gas, ozone-layer damage and the Montreal Protocol, climate treaties (Kyoto, Paris), acid rain gases, arsenic limits in Bangladesh, and ecology terms (ecosystem, food chain, 10% law).

## Ecology basics 🔥
- **Ecology** (term by **Ernst Haeckel, 1866**) studies the relationship between organisms and their environment. **Ecosystem** (term by **A. G. Tansley, 1935**) = living (biotic) + non-living (abiotic) parts working together.
- **Producers** (green plants) → **primary consumers** (herbivores) → **secondary consumers** (carnivores) → **tertiary consumers**. **Decomposers** (bacteria, fungi) return nutrients to soil.
- **Food chain** example: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk. Linked food chains form a **food web**.
- **10% law (Lindeman)**: only about **10% of energy** passes to the next trophic level; so food chains are short.
- **Sun is the ultimate source of energy** for ecosystems. Energy flow is **one-way**; nutrients **cycle**.
- For ecological balance a country should have about **25% of its land under forest**.

## Greenhouse effect and global warming (গ্রিনহাউস প্রভাব) 🔥🔥
- Sunlight (short-wave) passes through the air; the Earth re-emits **infrared (long-wave) heat**, which **greenhouse gases trap**, warming the planet. Without it, Earth's average temperature would be about **−18 °C** instead of ≈ **15 °C**.
- **Svante Arrhenius (1896)** first calculated warming from CO₂.

| Greenhouse gas | Main sources / fact |
|---|---|
| **Carbon dioxide (CO₂)** | **Main human-caused GHG**; burning fossil fuels, deforestation |
| **Methane (CH₄)** | **Rice paddies**, cattle, landfills, gas leaks; much stronger per molecule than CO₂ |
| **Nitrous oxide (N₂O)** | **Nitrogen fertilizers** |
| **CFCs**, HFCs | Refrigerators, ACs, aerosol sprays |
| **Water vapour** | Most abundant greenhouse gas (natural) |
| Ozone (lower atmosphere) | Smog |

- CO₂ was about **280 ppm before the Industrial Revolution** and passed **420 ppm around 2023** (Mauna Loa observatory).
- Effects: **sea-level rise**, melting glaciers, stronger cyclones, salinity intrusion, floods, droughts. **Bangladesh is one of the most climate-vulnerable countries** (low-lying coastal delta).

> 🔄 Update: check the latest CO₂ concentration and global temperature records in a newspaper or the WMO/NOAA reports.

## Ozone layer (ওজোন স্তর) 🔥🔥
- Ozone (**O₃**) is concentrated in the **stratosphere** (≈ 15–35 km); it **absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV-B) rays** that cause skin cancer and cataracts.
- Measured in **Dobson units (DU)**.
- Destroyed mainly by **CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons)**, which release **chlorine**; also halons, carbon tetrachloride.
- **Ozone hole over Antarctica** was reported in **1985** (British Antarctic Survey).
- **Vienna Convention (1985)** → **Montreal Protocol (1987)** to phase out ozone-depleting substances. **World Ozone Day: 16 September**. **Kigali Amendment (2016)** adds **HFCs**.
- Ozone near the ground is a **pollutant** (smog).

| **Stockholm Conference**; **UNEP** founded (HQ **Nairobi**) | **1972**; **World Environment Day 5 June** |
| **IPCC** (by WMO & UNEP) | **1988** |
| **Earth Summit, Rio de Janeiro** → **UNFCCC** | **1992** |
| **Kyoto Protocol** (binding cuts for developed countries) | Adopted **1997**, in force **2005** |
| **Paris Agreement** (COP21) — keep warming **well below 2 °C, aim 1.5 °C** | Adopted **December 2015**, in force **4 November 2016** |
| **COP29** (Baku, Azerbaijan) | 2024 — climate finance goal |
| **COP30** (Belém, Brazil) | November 2025 |
| Earth Day | 22 April |

> 🔄 Update: check the host and outcome of the latest COP in a newspaper.

## Pollution (দূষণ) 🔥
| Pollutant | Source | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Carbon monoxide (CO)** | Vehicle exhaust, incomplete burning | **Binds haemoglobin** → oxygen shortage, death |
| **SO₂ and NOₓ** | Coal, oil burning, vehicles, brick kilns | **Acid rain** (pH < 5.6), respiratory disease |
| **Particulate matter (PM2.5, PM10)** | Dust, brick kilns, vehicles | Lung and heart disease; Dhaka often among the world's most polluted cities |
| **Lead** | Old petrol, batteries, paint | Brain damage in children |
| **Smog** | Smoke + fog | Poor visibility, breathing trouble |
| **Nitrates/phosphates** (fertilizer runoff) | Farms, sewage | **Eutrophication** — algal bloom, fish die (low oxygen) |
| **Mercury** | Industry | **Minamata disease** (Japan) |
| **Cadmium** | Mining | **Itai-itai disease** (Japan) |
| **Methyl isocyanate (MIC)** | Pesticide plant | **Bhopal gas tragedy, India (1984)** |

- **BOD (biochemical oxygen demand)** measures organic water pollution: higher BOD = more polluted.
- **Noise** is measured in **decibels (dB)**; long exposure above ≈ 85 dB harms hearing.

## Bangladesh environment facts 🔥
- **Arsenic in groundwater**: first detected in **1993** (Chapai Nawabganj). **WHO guideline: 0.01 mg/L (10 µg/L)**; **Bangladesh standard: 0.05 mg/L (50 µg/L)**. It causes **arsenicosis** (skin lesions, cancer).
- **Department of Environment** set up in **1989**; **Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act 1995**.
- **Polythene shopping bags banned in 2002**.
- **Bangladesh Climate Change Strategy and Action Plan (BCCSAP) 2009**; **Climate Change Trust Fund** created from Bangladesh's own budget (2009–10).
- Major pollution sources: brick kilns, vehicles, tanneries (moved from Hazaribagh to **Savar** tannery estate), textile dyeing, plastic waste.

## Quick revision
- **CO₂ = main greenhouse gas** from human activity; water vapour is the most abundant.
- Methane from **rice fields and cattle**; N₂O from fertilizers.
- **Ozone layer in the stratosphere** absorbs UV; destroyed by **CFCs**.
- **Montreal Protocol 1987**; Kyoto 1997; **Paris 2015** (1.5–2 °C).
- **Acid rain: SO₂ + NOₓ**; CO binds haemoglobin.
- **Eutrophication** = excess nutrients → algal bloom.
- Arsenic limit: **WHO 0.01 mg/L, Bangladesh 0.05 mg/L**.
- World Environment Day **5 June**; Ozone Day **16 September**; UNEP HQ **Nairobi**.

## The Sun and the solar system 🔥
- The **Sun** is a medium-sized **star**, about **4.6 billion years** old, made mostly of **hydrogen (≈ 73%) and helium**. Its energy comes from **nuclear fusion**. Surface ≈ **5,500–6,000 °C**; core ≈ **15 million °C**. It holds ≈ **99.8%** of the solar system's mass.
- Sunlight reaches Earth in **≈ 8 min 20 s**; mean Earth–Sun distance = **1 AU ≈ 15 crore km (149.6 million km)**.
- **Heliocentric theory** (Sun at the centre): **Nicolaus Copernicus (1543)**. Ptolemy had given the geocentric model. **Galileo** (1609–10) used a telescope and found **4 large moons of Jupiter**. **Kepler** gave the laws of planetary motion.
- **8 planets**. **Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet on 24 August 2006** by the IAU (Prague). Other dwarf planets: **Ceres, Eris, Haumea, Makemake**.
- Order from the Sun: **Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune**. (Hook: *My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Nuts*.) Inner four are rocky; outer four are gas/ice giants.

## Planet facts 🔥🔥

| **Mercury (বুধ)** | **Smallest** planet, **closest to the Sun**; **shortest year (88 days)**; no moon |
| **Venus (শুক্র)** | **Hottest planet (≈ 465 °C)** due to thick CO₂ atmosphere; **brightest planet**; **"morning star / evening star" (শুকতারা/সন্ধ্যাতারা)**; rotates **east to west (retrograde)**; its **day (243 Earth days) is longer than its year (225 days)**; no moon; "Earth's twin" in size |
| **Earth (পৃথিবী)** | **Densest planet**; only known life; "blue planet"; 1 moon; rotation ≈ 23 h 56 min; year 365¼ days; axis tilted **23.5°** |
| **Mars (মঙ্গল)** | **"Red planet"** (iron oxide dust); moons **Phobos and Deimos**; **Olympus Mons** — highest volcano in the solar system |
| **Jupiter (বৃহস্পতি)** | **Largest and most massive**; **fastest rotation (≈ 10 hours)**; **Great Red Spot** (giant storm); moon **Ganymede = largest moon** of the solar system |
| **Saturn (শনি)** | **Most prominent rings**; **least dense** (would float on water); largest moon **Titan** (thick atmosphere); **most known moons** (274 recognised as of 2025) |
| **Uranus (ইউরেনাস)** | Discovered by **William Herschel (1781)** — first planet found with a telescope; **rotates on its side** (≈ 98° tilt); greenish-blue (methane) |
| **Neptune (নেপচুন)** | **Farthest planet**; found in **1846** (predicted mathematically by Le Verrier and Adams, seen by Galle); **strongest winds**; year ≈ 165 Earth years. Many guides call it the coldest planet (Uranus actually has the lowest recorded temperature) |

- **Asteroid belt**: between **Mars and Jupiter**; **Ceres** is the largest object there.
- **Halley's Comet**: returns about every **76 years**; last seen **1986**, next **2061**.

## The Moon (চাঁদ) 🔥
- Average distance **≈ 3,84,400 km**; diameter ≈ **3,474 km** (≈ ¼ of Earth's).
- Orbits Earth in **≈ 27.3 days** (sidereal); new moon to new moon **≈ 29.5 days**. We always see the **same face** (rotation = revolution period).
- **No atmosphere**, so no sound, sky looks black; **gravity ≈ 1/6** of Earth's. Moonlight takes **≈ 1.3 s** to reach Earth.
- **Tides** are caused mainly by the Moon's gravity (the Sun also helps; spring tides at new/full moon).
- **Solar eclipse** occurs on a **new moon (অমাবস্যা)** day; **lunar eclipse** on a **full moon (পূর্ণিমা)** night.

## Stars and galaxies
- We live in the **Milky Way (আকাশগঙ্গা / ছায়াপথ)**, a **spiral galaxy**. The nearest large galaxy is **Andromeda**.
- **Nearest star after the Sun: Proxima Centauri (≈ 4.2 light-years)**. **Brightest star in the night sky: Sirius**. **Pole star: Polaris (ধ্রুবতারা)**.
- **Big Bang theory**: Georges Lemaître; **Edwin Hubble (1929)** showed the universe is expanding. The **first image of a black hole** (M87*) was released in **2019** by the Event Horizon Telescope.

SCI-25.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask the composition of air, which layer has weather/ozone/radio reflection, the coldest layer, rock types with examples (granite, marble), Earth's interior, earthquake waves and the Richter scale.

## Composition of air 🔥
| Gas | Share by volume |
|---|---|
| **Nitrogen (N₂)** | **≈ 78%** |
| **Oxygen (O₂)** | **≈ 21%** |
| **Argon (Ar)** | **≈ 0.93%** (most abundant noble gas in air) |
| **Carbon dioxide (CO₂)** | **≈ 0.04%** |
| Others | Neon, helium, methane, krypton, hydrogen, ozone; plus variable **water vapour** and dust |

- Standard atmospheric pressure = **1,013 millibar = 76 cm of mercury**; pressure and density fall with height. About **half the air's mass lies below ≈ 5.5 km**.

## Layers of the atmosphere (বায়ুমণ্ডলের স্তর) 🔥🔥
| Layer (from ground) | Approx. height | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| **Troposphere (ট্রপোমণ্ডল)** | 0 – **≈ 8 km at poles, ≈ 18 km at equator** (average ≈ 12 km) | **All weather**: clouds, rain, storms; contains most water vapour and dust. Temperature **falls ≈ 6.5 °C per km** (lapse rate). Upper boundary: **tropopause** |
| **Stratosphere (স্ট্রাটোমণ্ডল)** | ≈ 18 – **50 km** | Contains the **ozone layer** (≈ 15–35 km); temperature **rises** with height; calm, no clouds — **jet aircraft** fly in its lower part |
| **Mesosphere (মেসোমণ্ডল)** | ≈ 50 – **80/85 km** | **Coldest layer** (≈ −90 °C at the top); **meteors burn up** here |
| **Thermosphere (তাপমণ্ডল)** | ≈ 80 – 600 km | Very high temperature; contains the **ionosphere**; **aurora** (northern/southern lights) |
| **Exosphere (বহিঃমণ্ডল)** | Above ≈ 600 km | Outermost; thin, merges into space; light gases (H, He) |

- **Ionosphere** (≈ 80–400 km, mainly in the thermosphere) has charged particles that **reflect radio waves** back to Earth, allowing long-distance radio communication. Its layers include the **Kennelly–Heaviside (E) layer** and the **Appleton (F) layer**.
- **Satellites** (including the ISS at ≈ 400 km) orbit in the thermosphere/exosphere.

## Weather quick facts
- Planetary winds: **trade winds**, **westerlies**, polar easterlies. The **Coriolis effect** deflects winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere.
- **Tropical cyclones** turn **anticlockwise** in the Northern Hemisphere; the calm centre is the **eye**. Names by region: **cyclone** (Bay of Bengal/Indian Ocean), **hurricane** (Atlantic/East Pacific), **typhoon** (West Pacific).
- In Bangladesh's maritime ports, signals run from **1 to 11**; **5–7 = danger**, **8–10 = great danger**, **11 = communication failure**.
- Highest clouds: **cirrus**; thunderstorm cloud: **cumulonimbus**.

## Interior of the Earth 🔥
| Layer | Facts |
|---|---|
| **Crust (ভূত্বক)** | Thinnest; ≈ **5–10 km under oceans**, ≈ **30–70 km under continents**. Upper continental part: **SIAL** (silicon + aluminium); ocean floor/lower part: **SIMA** (silicon + magnesium) |
| **Mantle (গুরুমণ্ডল)** | To ≈ **2,900 km**; largest by volume; source of magma |
| **Outer core** | **Liquid** iron–nickel |
| **Inner core** | **Solid** iron–nickel (**NiFe**), ≈ 5,000–6,000 °C |

- **Mohorovičić (Moho) discontinuity**: between crust and mantle. **Gutenberg discontinuity**: between mantle and core.
- Earth's mean radius ≈ **6,371 km** (equatorial ≈ 6,378 km).

## Rocks (শিলা) 🔥🔥
| Type | How formed | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Igneous (আগ্নেয় শিলা)** — "**primary rock**" | Cooling of **magma/lava** | **Granite** (cooled slowly inside Earth), **basalt** (lava on surface), gabbro, pumice |
| **Sedimentary (পাললিক শিলা)** | Layers of sediment pressed together; may contain **fossils** | **Sandstone, limestone, shale, conglomerate, coal**, clay |
| **Metamorphic (রূপান্তরিত শিলা)** | Existing rocks changed by **heat and pressure** | **Limestone → marble**, **sandstone → quartzite**, **shale → slate**, **granite → gneiss**, **coal → graphite**, slate → schist |

- **Fossils** and **petroleum/coal** are found in **sedimentary rocks**.
- **Bangladesh** is mostly made of **sedimentary (alluvial) deposits** of the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta. **Hard igneous rock (granite)** is mined at **Maddhapara, Dinajpur**.

## Plate tectonics and earthquakes (ভূমিকম্প) 🔥🔥
- **Alfred Wegener (1912)** proposed **continental drift**; all continents were once one supercontinent, **Pangaea**. **Plate tectonics** (1960s) explains earthquakes and volcanoes at plate boundaries.
- Bangladesh lies near the meeting of the **Indian, Eurasian and Burma plates**; the **north-eastern region (Sylhet, Mymensingh)** is the most earthquake-prone.
- **Focus (hypocentre)**: where the earthquake starts inside the Earth. **Epicentre (উপকেন্দ্র)**: point on the surface **directly above** the focus.

| Seismic wave | Features |
|---|---|
| **P-wave (primary)** | **Fastest**, arrives first; **longitudinal**; passes through solids and liquids |
| **S-wave (secondary)** | **Transverse**; **cannot pass through liquid** → proof that the **outer core is liquid** |
| **L-wave / surface waves** | Slowest; travel along the surface; **most destructive** |

- Recorded by a **seismograph**. **Richter scale (Charles Richter, 1935)** measures **magnitude**; it is **logarithmic** — each whole number = **10 times** the ground-shaking amplitude and ≈ **32 times** the energy. Scientists now use the **moment magnitude scale**. The **Mercalli scale** measures **intensity (damage)**.
- **Tsunami** (Japanese for "harbour wave") is caused mainly by **undersea earthquakes**. **Indian Ocean tsunami: 26 December 2004** (Sumatra, magnitude ≈ 9.1).
- **Pacific "Ring of Fire"** has most of the world's earthquakes and active volcanoes.
- Notable earthquakes: **Great Assam earthquake 1897** (hit this region hard); **Nepal, 25 April 2015 (M 7.8)**; **Türkiye–Syria, 6 February 2023 (M 7.8)**; **Myanmar (Mandalay region), 28 March 2025 (M 7.7)**, felt in Bangladesh.
- Volcanoes: **active, dormant, extinct**. **Vesuvius** buried **Pompeii (79 CE)**; **Krakatoa (1883)** eruption; **Mauna Loa (Hawaii)** is the largest active volcano.

## Quick revision
- Air: **N₂ 78%, O₂ 21%, Ar 0.93%, CO₂ 0.04%**.
- **Troposphere = weather; stratosphere = ozone & jet planes; mesosphere = coldest, meteors burn; thermosphere/ionosphere = radio reflection & aurora.**
- Temperature falls ≈ **6.5 °C/km** in the troposphere.
- **Granite & basalt = igneous; limestone & sandstone = sedimentary; marble & slate = metamorphic.**
- **Limestone → marble; shale → slate; sandstone → quartzite.**
- Core: iron–nickel; **outer core liquid** (S-waves stop).
- **Epicentre** is above the focus; **Richter scale** (logarithmic) measures magnitude.
- Continental drift: **Wegener**; Pangaea.

SCI-27.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask renewable vs non-renewable sources, what a solar cell is made of, Bangladesh's only hydroelectric plant (Kaptai), biogas composition, SREDA/IDCOL, and nanotechnology basics (1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m, Feynman, carbon nanotubes, uses).

## Renewable vs non-renewable energy 🔥
| Renewable (নবায়নযোগ্য) | Non-renewable (অনবায়নযোগ্য) |
|---|---|
| **Solar, wind, hydro (water), biomass, biogas, geothermal, tidal, wave**, green hydrogen | **Coal, petroleum, natural gas** (fossil fuels), **nuclear fuel (uranium)** |
| Naturally replenished; low carbon emission | Limited stock; fossil fuels emit CO₂ |

- The **Sun** is the ultimate source of almost all energy on Earth (except nuclear, geothermal and tidal).

## Solar energy (সৌরশক্তি) 🔥🔥
- **Solar cell (photovoltaic cell)** converts **sunlight directly into electricity** (DC) by the **photovoltaic effect** (first observed by **Edmond Becquerel, 1839**).
- Most solar cells are made of **silicon** (a semiconductor). The first practical silicon solar cell was made at **Bell Labs in 1954**. Commercial panels are about **15–22% efficient**.
- Solar panels + **battery + charge controller + inverter** (DC → AC) make a solar home system.
- **Solar water heaters and solar cookers** use sunlight as heat (solar thermal).
- **Bangladesh**: the **Solar Home System (SHS)** programme, financed mainly through **IDCOL** (Infrastructure Development Company Ltd), installed **millions (≈ 6 million)** of systems in off-grid rural homes — one of the **largest off-grid solar programmes in the world**. Solar irrigation pumps and rooftop solar with **net metering (guideline 2018)** are expanding.
- Largest solar park in Bangladesh (as of 2023): **Teesta solar plant, Sundarganj, Gaibandha (≈ 200 MW)**.

## Other renewable sources 🔥
| Source | Key facts |
|---|---|
| **Hydroelectric (জলবিদ্যুৎ)** | Potential energy of stored water → turbine → electricity. **Kaptai Hydroelectric Plant** on the **Karnaphuli river, Rangamati** — **Bangladesh's only hydropower plant**; started in **1962**; capacity ≈ **230 MW** |
| **Wind (বায়ু)** | Wind turbines; best at coasts and open areas. Early Bangladesh projects: **Sonagazi (Feni)** and **Kutubdia (Cox's Bazar)**; a ≈ **60 MW** wind farm at **Khurushkul, Cox's Bazar** began supplying the grid in 2023. China leads the world in solar and wind |
| **Biogas (বায়োগ্যাস)** | From **cow dung**, kitchen and poultry waste by **anaerobic** bacteria; **≈ 55–70% methane (CH₄)**, rest mostly CO₂; leftover **slurry is good fertilizer** |
| **Biomass** | Wood, crop residue, rice husk, jute sticks; bio-ethanol, biodiesel |
| **Geothermal (ভূ-তাপ)** | Heat from inside the Earth; **Iceland**, Philippines, USA, Indonesia use it widely |
| **Tidal (জোয়ার-ভাটা)** | **La Rance, France (1966)** — first large tidal power station; Sihwa Lake (South Korea) is the largest |
| **Hydrogen / fuel cell** | Fuel cell combines H₂ and O₂ → **electricity + water** (no pollution). **Green hydrogen** is made by electrolysis using renewable power |

## Institutions and policy 🔥
| Body | Fact |
|---|---|
| **SREDA** (Sustainable and Renewable Energy Development Authority) | Bangladesh's nodal agency for renewables and energy efficiency, set up in **2014** (Act 2012) |
| **IDCOL** | Finances SHS, solar irrigation, biogas plants |
| **Renewable Energy Policy (2008)** | Bangladesh's first; aimed for 10% of power from renewables by 2020 (not achieved) |
| **IRENA** (International Renewable Energy Agency) | Founded **2009**; HQ **Abu Dhabi**, UAE |
| **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** | Launched **2015** by **India and France** at COP21; HQ **Gurugram, India** |

- Renewables still make up only a **small share** of Bangladesh's electricity; natural gas remains the main source.

> 🔄 Update: check the latest renewable share, installed solar/wind capacity and the newest renewable energy policy targets in a newspaper or the Bangladesh Economic Review.

## Nanotechnology (ন্যানোপ্রযুক্তি) 🔥🔥
- **"Nano"** comes from the Greek *nanos* = **dwarf**. **1 nanometre (nm) = 10⁻⁹ m** (one billionth of a metre).
- Nanotechnology works with materials at about **1–100 nm**, where they show new properties (colour, strength, conductivity, reactivity) because of large surface area and quantum effects.
- **Richard Feynman**'s 1959 lecture ***"There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom"*** first described the idea → he is called the **father of nanotechnology**. The term **"nanotechnology"** was coined by **Norio Taniguchi (1974)**; **K. Eric Drexler** popularised it (*Engines of Creation*, 1986).
- Scale sense: a human hair is ≈ **80,000–100,000 nm** thick; DNA double helix ≈ **2 nm** wide.
- **Approaches**: **top-down** (cutting bulk material smaller, e.g. chip lithography) and **bottom-up** (building from atoms/molecules, self-assembly).

| Tool / material | Fact |
|---|---|
| **Scanning tunnelling microscope (STM)** | **Binnig & Rohrer (1981)**, Nobel 1986 — "see" and move single atoms |
| Atomic force microscope (AFM) | 1986 |
| **Fullerene (C₆₀)** | 1985 |
| **Carbon nanotube** | **Sumio Iijima (1991)** — very strong, light, conducts electricity |
| **Graphene** | 2004, Geim & Novoselov (Nobel 2010) — one-atom-thick carbon |
| **Quantum dots** | Nobel Chemistry **2023** (Bawendi, Brus, Ekimov) — QLED TV screens, bio-imaging |

**Uses of nanotechnology:**
- **Medicine**: **targeted drug delivery** (e.g. cancer drugs), nano-sensors for diagnosis, antibacterial **silver nanoparticles** in dressings.
- **Cosmetics**: **zinc oxide and titanium dioxide nanoparticles** in **sunscreens** (transparent UV blockers).
- **Electronics**: smaller, faster chips (transistors a few nm in size), memory, displays.
- **Energy and environment**: better solar cells and batteries, water filters, **self-cleaning glass**, stain-resistant fabrics.
- **Materials**: stronger, lighter composites (sports goods, cars, aircraft).
- **Concerns**: possible toxicity of nanoparticles to health and environment.

## Quick revision
- Renewable: **solar, wind, hydro, biomass, biogas, geothermal, tidal**; nuclear is **non-renewable**.
- **Solar cell = silicon**, photovoltaic effect, gives DC; inverter converts DC → AC.
- **Kaptai (Karnaphuli, Rangamati)** = Bangladesh's only hydropower plant (1962, ≈230 MW).
- **Biogas ≈ 60% methane**, made anaerobically from cow dung.
- **SREDA (2014)**; IDCOL funds solar home systems; IRENA HQ **Abu Dhabi**.
- **1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m**; nanoscale **1–100 nm**; nano = dwarf.
- **Feynman (1959)** idea; **Taniguchi (1974)** coined the term; STM 1981.
- Carbon nanotube: **Iijima (1991)**; ZnO/TiO₂ nanoparticles in sunscreens.

SCI-28.notes:
> **Why it matters:** Exams ask what each machine uses (X-ray, magnet, sound, electrical signals), who invented it, what it diagnoses, which ones use harmful radiation, and normal clinical values (pulse, BP, SpO₂).

## Imaging machines at a glance 🔥🔥🔥
| Technique | What it uses | Best for | Inventor / Nobel |
|---|---|---|---|
| **X-ray (রঞ্জন রশ্মি)** | **X-rays** (ionising EM waves) | **Bone fractures**, chest (**TB, pneumonia**), teeth, mammography | **Wilhelm Röntgen, 8 November 1895** (first Nobel in Physics, 1901) |
| **CT / CAT scan** (computed tomography) | **X-rays from many angles + computer** → cross-sectional images | **Head injury, stroke**, tumours, internal bleeding | **Godfrey Hounsfield & Allan Cormack** (Nobel Medicine **1979**); first scanner early 1970s |
| **MRI** (magnetic resonance imaging) | **Strong magnetic field + radio waves** (acts on **hydrogen nuclei** in body water); **no ionising radiation** | **Soft tissues: brain, spinal cord, joints, ligaments**, tumours | **Paul Lauterbur & Peter Mansfield** (Nobel Medicine **2003**); based on NMR (Bloch & Purcell) |
| **Ultrasonography (USG)** | **Ultrasound** (high-frequency sound, several MHz); **no radiation** | **Pregnancy (fetus)**, gallstones, liver, kidney, uterus | Developed in the 1950s (Ian Donald in obstetrics) |
| **Echocardiography** | Ultrasound of the **heart** | Heart valves, pumping | — |
| **Doppler ultrasound** | Doppler effect of sound | **Blood flow** in vessels | — |
| **PET scan** | **Radioactive tracer** (e.g. fluorine-18 glucose) emitting **positrons** | **Cancer spread**, brain activity | — |
| **Endoscopy** | **Optical fibre** (**total internal reflection**) with a camera | Inside **stomach**, food pipe, colon; also biopsy | — |
| **Angiography** | X-ray + **contrast dye** | **Blocked blood vessels** (coronary arteries) | — |

**Key points:**
- **X-ray and CT use ionising radiation** (risk with repeated exposure); **MRI and ultrasound do not**. Pregnant women are scanned by **ultrasound**, not X-ray.
- In an X-ray, **bones look white** because **calcium absorbs X-rays** strongly; soft tissue looks grey/dark. X-rays are produced in a **Coolidge tube** with a **tungsten** target. Staff wear **lead aprons**.
- **MRI** uses superconducting magnets (typically **1.5 or 3 tesla**) cooled by **liquid helium**. People with **pacemakers or some metal implants** may not be able to have an MRI.
- **Radiotherapy** for cancer uses **cobalt-60** gamma rays or a **linear accelerator (LINAC)**; **iodine-131** treats thyroid disease; **technetium-99m** is the most used diagnostic isotope.

## Recording the body's electrical signals 🔥
| Test | Records | Used for | Inventor |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ECG / EKG** (electrocardiogram) | **Electrical activity of the heart** | **Heart attack**, irregular heartbeat (arrhythmia) | **Willem Einthoven** (1903, string galvanometer; Nobel **1924**) |
| **EEG** (electroencephalogram) | **Electrical activity of the brain** | **Epilepsy**, sleep disorders, brain death | **Hans Berger** (1920s) |
| **EMG** (electromyogram) | Electrical activity of **muscles** | Nerve–muscle disorders | — |

- A normal ECG has a **P wave, QRS complex and T wave**. The **QRS complex** shows ventricular contraction.

## Life-support and therapeutic devices 🔥
| Device / procedure | Fact |
|---|---|
| **Artificial pacemaker** | Gives electrical pulses to keep the heartbeat regular; first implanted in **1958 (Sweden)** |
| **Dialysis machine ("artificial kidney")** | Filters blood when kidneys fail; developed by **Willem Kolff (1943)** |
| **Heart–lung machine** | Takes over heart and lung function during open-heart surgery; **John Gibbon (1953)** |
| **Angioplasty and stent** | A **balloon** opens a blocked coronary artery and a **stent** (mesh tube) keeps it open; first balloon angioplasty **Andreas Grüntzig (1977)** |
| **Bypass surgery (CABG)** | Uses a vessel graft to route blood around a blocked artery |
| **Ventilator** | Machine that helps or takes over **breathing** (ICU) |
| **Defibrillator** | Electric shock to restore normal heart rhythm |
| **LASIK** | **Laser** reshapes the cornea to correct vision |
| **Robotic surgery** | e.g. the da Vinci system; small cuts, high precision |
| **Gamma knife** | Focused gamma rays to treat brain tumours without opening the skull |

## Everyday clinical instruments and normal values 🔥🔥
| Instrument | Measures |
|---|---|
| **Stethoscope** (**René Laennec, 1816**) | Heart and lung sounds |
| **Sphygmomanometer** | **Blood pressure** (mmHg) |
| **Clinical thermometer** (Thomas Allbutt made a short, practical one, 1867) | Body temperature |
| **Pulse oximeter** | **Blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂)** and pulse, using red/infrared light through the fingertip |
| **Glucometer** | Blood glucose |
| **Audiometer** | Hearing |

| Measurement | Normal adult value |
|---|---|
| **Body temperature** | **37 °C = 98.4 °F (NCTB) / 98.6 °F** |
| **Pulse / heart rate** | **≈ 72 per minute** (60–100) |
| **Blood pressure** | **≈ 120/80 mmHg** |
| **Breathing rate** | **≈ 12–20 per minute** |
| **SpO₂** | **≈ 95–100%** |
| Fasting blood glucose | ≈ 3.9–5.5 mmol/L (70–100 mg/dL) |
| Blood pH | 7.35–7.45 |

- In Bangladesh, the **Institutes of Nuclear Medicine and Allied Sciences (INMAS)** under the **Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission** provide nuclear-medicine scans and treatment.

## Quick revision
- **X-ray: Röntgen (1895)**; bones look white because calcium absorbs X-rays.
- **CT = many X-rays + computer** (Hounsfield & Cormack, Nobel 1979).
- **MRI = magnet + radio waves**, no ionising radiation; best for **brain, spinal cord, soft tissue** (Nobel 2003).
- **Ultrasonography = high-frequency sound**; safe in **pregnancy**.
- **ECG = heart's electrical activity** (Einthoven); **EEG = brain** (Hans Berger).
- **Endoscopy** uses **optical fibre** (total internal reflection).
- Pacemaker keeps heartbeat regular; dialysis = artificial kidney (Kolff).
- Normal: **pulse 72/min, BP 120/80, SpO₂ 95–100%, temperature 37 °C**.
